name: Ancient Greek religion
title: The story of ancient Greek religion

text: More than 3,000 years ago, Greeks wrote the names of gods such as Zeus and Hera on clay tablets.
Later, the poets Homer and Hesiod told the stories of the gods that all Greeks shared.
src: the Mycenaean Greeks recorded offerings to their gods on clay tablets in the Linear B script / among the names are Zeus, Hera
The epics of Homer and the Theogony of Hesiod, composed around 700 BCE, became the shared foundation of Greek religion and myth

text: In the stories of the Greeks, twelve great gods lived on Mount Olympus, led by Zeus, god of the sky.
Poseidon was god of the sea, and Athena goddess of wisdom.
src: The twelve Olympians, who lived on Mount Olympus, were led by Zeus, god of the sky
his brother Poseidon, god of the sea and earthquakes / Athena, goddess of wisdom, war and crafts

text: Every city held festivals for its gods, with parades, music and sports.
In Athens, a parade carried a new robe to the old statue of Athena.
src: The city's year was marked by festivals / honoured Athena with a procession / with athletic and musical contests
In Athens the Panathenaia honoured Athena with a procession, shown on the frieze of the Parthenon, which brought a new robe for her ancient statue

text: Greek settlers carried their gods to new cities around the Mediterranean Sea.
Their temples at Paestum, in southern Italy, are among the best kept of the Greek world.
src: Greek religion travelled with Greek settlers, who from the 8th century BCE founded cities around the Mediterranean and the Black Sea
The temples of Paestum, Agrigento and Selinunte in southern Italy and Sicily are among the best preserved of the Greek world

text: Christian emperors banned the old worship more than 1,600 years ago.
But Roman poets such as Ovid passed on its stories, which are still told today.
src: Banned by the Christian emperors in the 390s / in 391 and 392 Theodosius I banned pagan sacrifice and worship
Through Roman poets such as Ovid, its gods and heroes passed into medieval and Renaissance literature and art / its stories remain among the most widely known in the world

text: The Olympic Games began as a festival for Zeus, and today's Games remember it.
Words such as hero and music, from the Muses, come from Greek religion.
src: The ancient Olympic Games were a religious festival of Zeus / the Olympic Games, revived in 1896, recall the athletic festivals held in honour of the gods
Words such as hero, mystery, theology, panic and music, from Pan and the Muses, come from Greek religion
